pageCache.pageTitle: Cotford St Luke Primary School - Welcome to Fledglings
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Fledglings
**Please note: Spaces in Fledglings are filling up quickly. If you are considering joining our lovely early years setting, please get in touch as soon as possible.**
Welcome to Fledglings
Fledglings Early Years Centre is located within Cotford St Luke Primary School and is managed by the school governors and Headteacher. Day-to-day operations are overseen by our Manager, Rebecca Batten.
We provide childcare for children aged 2 years and above, offering both full-day and sessional care from 8:00am to 4:00pm, five days a week, for 38 weeks of the year.
All children are welcome to attend our Breakfast Club from 8:00am to 8:45am.
Our pre-school sessions run from 8:45am to 3:15pm, with after-school care available from 3:15pm to 4:00pm.
We have five inset days each year dedicated to staff training, during which the centre is closed.
Fledglings features two dedicated learning spaces - Swifts for our 2-year-olds and Swallows for our 3-year-old - as well as a large, private garden shared by all children.
We also make full use of the school’s facilities, including the adjacent outdoor area with a large play mound, a weekly hall slot, access to iPads, and use of the school playground.
Throughout the year, we join in with whole-school events such as Remembrance Day, Christmas performances, and Sports Day.
Our doors open directly into the Reception classroom, and when it is safe to do so, we operate an open-door environment where Swallows and Oak Class (Reception) children can choose where they would like to play and learn.
We are very pleased to announce that, in October 2025, we were awarded a 5* Hygiene Rating from the Food Standards Agency - we are delighted with this outcome.
All of Fledglings staff have recently completed (March 2024) a minimum of 15 hours of Dingley's Promise training. This has enabled them to gain a mark of achievement as an Inclusion Friendly Setting.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cotford St Luke Primary School - Wraparound Care
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care at Cotford St Luke School is provided by Premier Education
Please see their information below about what is on offer and details of how to book.
Premier Education is a local organisation that works closely with schools to support families by delivering high-quality Breakfast and Afterschool Club provision. Our wraparound care offers children a safe, engaging, and enjoyable start and end to their school day.
We offer a wide range of sporting activities, all delivered by fully qualified and compliant sports coaches. Our sports timetable changes daily, so we encourage families to check activities when booking.
Alongside sport, children can enjoy a variety of creative craft activities, with a new theme each week inspired by popular children’s books. These themed sessions encourage children to explore different techniques, spark their imagination, and develop their creativity.
Children attending Breakfast Club and full Afterschool Club sessions are also provided with a selection of balanced, nutritious snacks to keep them energised and ready for the rest of the day.
We are also Ofsted registered and allow all types of childcare vouchers
We’re proud to support the school community and look forward to continuing to work with families and children throughout the year.
To book or view session times, dates and prices please see - https://www.premier-education.com/parents/venue/courses/18138/

pageCache.pageTitle: Cotford St Luke Primary School - Reception and KS1 Enjoy a Wonderful Day at Court Farm
pageCache.text:
Reception and KS1 Enjoy a Wonderful Day at Court Farm
On 8th July, our children from Reception and KS1 had a fantastic day out at Court Farm. The children had the opportunity to see and learn about lots of different animals, making some wonderful memories along the way.
The excitement continued with fun tractor rides, which were a highlight of the day and brought lots of smiles and laughter. It was a truly enjoyable experience, filled with exploration, discovery and plenty of fun.
We were incredibly proud of how well the children coped in the warm weather. They showed excellent behaviour, listened carefully to instructions and represented our school beautifully throughout the trip. T
A big thank you to all the children for making the trip so special and to the staff who helped make the day such a success.

EY Curricular Goals
Monster Phonics
At Fledglings, we follow and use the Monster Phonics scheme to support children’s early phonics development. Monster Phonics is a fun, multi-sensory approach that helps children to recognise sounds and begin developing early reading skills through colour-coding, actions and engaging activities.
As this scheme is also used by the teachers and children throughout the main school, introducing Monster Phonics in Fledglings provides valuable continuity and supports a smooth transition into Reception. By embedding this approach into our daily practice, we help children build confidence and familiarity with phonics from an early age, giving them a strong foundation for future learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cotford St Luke Primary School - Early Years Entitlement
pageCache.text:
Early Years Entitlement
3 - 4 Year Olds - Early Years Entitlement
All children aged 3 and 4 years are entitled to 15 hours of free Early Years Entitlement (EYE) childcare per week for 38 weeks of the year, regardless of family income or working status.
At Fledglings, we will apply for this funding on your behalf. To enable us to do so, we will need to see a copy of your child’s birth certificate and ask you to complete and sign a funding declaration form. Please speak to a member of the Fledglings team for further information.
Eligible working parents of 3 and 4 year olds can access up to 30 hours of funded childcare per week (maximum 10 hours per day). To qualify, each parent must earn the equivalent of at least 16 hours per week at the National Minimum or Living Wage (or be self-employed), and earn less than £100,000 per year.
If you are eligible, you will need to apply online (Apply Here) and provide Fledglings with your 30-hour code and National Insurance number. Parents are responsible for reconfirming their eligibility every three months. If a code expires, funded hours may be charged.
Please use the following website to work out when it is best for you to apply for funding. When should I apply for funding?
Funding for 2 Year Olds
Some 2 year olds are entitled to 15 hours of funded childcare if families meet certain criteria, such as receiving qualifying benefits. This funding is available for 38 weeks of the year and can be used in the same way as funding for 3 and 4 year olds.
In addition, eligible working parents of 2 year olds can now access up to 30 hours of funded childcare per week under the expanded Early Years Entitlement. Eligibility criteria are the same as for 30-hour funding for 3 and 4 year olds.
Parents must apply online (Apply Here) and provide their funding code to Fledglings. Eligibility must be reconfirmed every three months.
Important Information
Funding is provided for 38 weeks per year - please note, we are open for 39 weeks!
Additional hours and optional extras may be charged
Parents are responsible for applying for and reconfirming eligibility for working-parent entitlements
At Fledglings, we are pleased to accept funded places for 2, 3 and 4 year olds, subject to availability.
If you would like further advice or support with applying for funding, please speak to Rebecca or a member of the Fledglings Team, who will be happy to help.
Funding Terms & When to Apply
Spring Term: 1st January - 31st March
Summer Term: 1st April - 31st August
Autumn Term: 1st September - 31st December
Your child’s birthday
When they can get their hours from
Recommended time to apply
Term starting on or after 1 Jan (Spring term)

You can use your child's hours in two different settings but it is important that we are made aware of this so that we can ensure both settings are claiming the correct hours.
Tax Free Childcare, Tax Credits and other Childcare Choices
There are a number of new childcare payment options for parents. If you are working, you may be eligible for tax-free childcare, 30 hours of funding or tax credits towards the cost of your childcare. The governments' Childcare Choices gives a clear description of the options with tools for application:- Childcare Choices
You can find out about what childcare options are available locally and apply for funding on the Somerset.Gov Government Website - Tax-Free Childcare
The 15 and 30 hours free childcare is not intended to cover the cost of chargeable extras. At Fledglings, we are transparent about any optional, chargeable extras, which may include gymnastics sessions, Forest School activities, nursery trips and hot dinners.
These extras are entirely optional and are not a condition of your child's nursery place. Participation is always at the discretion of parents and carers and families are free to choose whether or not to take up these additional opportunities.
Further information, including costs and how to opt in, will be shared with parents and carers in advance where applicable.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cotford St Luke Primary School - Forest School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
Forest School at Fledglings
We are very fortunate to have a weekly Forest School session in our on-site Forest School area. Located at the back of the school, this space is a small mixed woodland made up of oak, hazel and beech trees, providing a rich and stimulating natural environment for learning and play.
Our Forest School area includes a shelter, fire pit and pond. The gently sloped ground offers plenty of opportunities to challenge and develop children’s physical skills, confidence and resilience, while encouraging exploration and adventurous play.
Forest School sessions support hands-on, child-led learning and allow children to explore the natural world through a wide range of practical and creative activities, including:
Forest School encourages curiosity, independence and teamwork, while helping children develop a love and respect for the natural environment.
Pond dipping
Bug hunts and building bug hotels
Sawing and safe tool use
Flower and leaf pressing
Creating clay models
Natural painting
Tree and leaf spotting
Collecting sticks and learning about fire safety
Making hot chocolate using a Kelly Kettle
Swinging in the hammock
